Subject: Aurelia: per-tenant model-affinity control — prioritization request

Team — forwarding a customer ask that has become a gating item for a close we expect in three weeks. Short summary up front and then the customer message below.

Ask (what we need):
- A small control that pins a tenant to a model affinity variant (e.g., force model-x-q4 for all requests for that tenant) and an API flag to opt into it.
- A short canary path + fallback so if the pinned variant is unavailable the request falls back to the platform default.

Why: Aurelia's procurement and security teams require per-tenant model binding to satisfy their audit & explainability controls (they must be able to say which variant served production inference). They will only sign a 3-year committed contract if we can guarantee this capability or a practicable equivalent.

Timeline constraints: procurement wants the SOW signed by 2027-12-05; engineering delivery would need to be gated for a customer pilot week-of 2027-11-29 to allow integration and compliance testing.

Impact / tradeoffs:
- This is scoped as a small runtime switch + router policy + API flag rather than a full tenant-residency feature, but it does require a minor change to the routing policy and the config model.
- If we can provide this with a documented fallback and an opt-in EULA clause, procurement may accept.

Attachments: Aurelia sent an updated SOW and a requirements spreadsheet (attached). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/987654321/AURE-2027-112

Questions for Product/Eng:
1) Marissa — can product sign off on a scope limited to an API flag + router pin + fallback? What needs product review?
2) Karthik — rough T-shirt estimate and whether this can be squeezed into a 1-2 sprint small scoped change with a canary? Any blockers we should know now?
3) Ben — I'll loop CS for integration once we have an implementation plan; is there anything on the support/process side to prepare for a customer opt-in pilot?

Appreciate a quick read — procurement timeline is tight.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Aurelia: per-tenant model-affinity control — prioritization request

Quick feasibility note from Eng:

- Implementation sketch: add a tenant-config key (model_affinity_pin) consumed by the router. Router reads the key and bypasses normal affinity heuristics when set. Persist config in existing tenant config store, emit trace annotations and write an audit event. Add fallback: if pinned model not available, return header X-Model-Fallback: true and route to default variant.
- Estimated effort: 5 dev-days + 2 QA-days + 1 day Docs + 1 infra-day for trace/audit plumbing => roughly 2 calendar weeks if we can prioritize immediate sprint capacity. If queued behind other work it'll slip to 4+ weeks.
- Risk: routing complexity is low; audit/tracing plumbing is the bigger chunk. No infra-level security change needed.

If Product can provide ACs this sprint, we can scope a minimal MVP and cut a canary build for Aurelia in ~10 business days.

Karthik
Eng Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
